strengths: The exact v3 pixels preserve the broad Home spatial language: a large soft seating/bed-like mass remains on the left and the desk/lamp zone remains on the right, so the room still reads as the same basic bedroom layout rather than a different environment.
Warm light continues to enter from the left and the pink/lilac base with cyan/turquoise and gold accents is cohesive, attractive and child-appropriate.
Rounded furniture forms, clean matte surfaces and soft lighting provide a convincing premium toy/diorama foundation rather than the rejected flat-vector look.
The environment remains separable scene art with no baked avatar, UI, counters, cards, text or equipped-state assumptions.

The exact 390x844 derivative shows no obvious asset corruption, broken decode, pixel damage or unusable crop artifact at the image level; this does not pre-empt reviewer 14's phone composition/performance judgment.
reworkReasons: The authoritative Home reference is materially richer and more recognizable as the same personalized bedroom: it has an explicit large left window, an unmistakable bed with pink bedding, shelves/books, wall art/posters, string/fairy lighting and numerous small decorative/activity objects. V3 strips too much of that authored identity away and reads as a sparse generic pastel room.

The left hero furniture reads more like a plush couch/daybed than the reference's clear bed. That furniture-type drift weakens immediate Home-room recognition even though the left/right layout remains correct.
The reference window is a visible architectural element with framing and a clear daylight source. V3 mostly implies the opening through warm light, so an important architecture cue has been lost.

Material separation is too uniform. V3 relies heavily on smooth matte treatment, while the reference layers textile bedding, harder shelf/furniture surfaces, metallic lighting/decor and varied small-object finishes. The current scene needs more tactile differentiation without becoming photorealistic.

Color is harmonized but too muted relative to the authoritative Home pixels. The reference carries stronger saturated pink/purple/blue/yellow accents and decorative light points; v3's quieter pastel treatment reduces the magical-school/game-world energy.

The previous reviewer-01 v1 contract explicitly required approximately 4-7 secondary environmental props and stronger game-specific density in the side zones. The v3 composition repair successfully prioritizes a quieter hero corridor, but it does not satisfy that art/fidelity density requirement; the two goals should be solved together rather than trading one for the other.
boundedRepairContract: Preserve v3's successful lower/central quiet corridor, left-side warm light direction, bed-left/desk-right macro-layout and separate-background architecture. Do not solve fidelity by refilling the center hero corridor.

Make the left furniture unmistakably a bed: readable mattress/bedding volume, pillows and bed-frame/headboard language, while keeping its mass constrained to the left side so reviewer 14's composition repair is not undone.
Restore an explicit left-side window/opening with visible frame/depth and daylight, but keep its brightest hotspot outside the avatar-safe center corridor.

Add roughly 4-7 distinct reference-grounded secondary props only in side/perimeter zones: shelf/books, small collectibles, wall art/posters without readable text, fairy/string lights, and one or two activity/decor objects. Preserve calm overlay zones and no UI-like marks.

Increase material differentiation: visibly soft bedding/textiles, firmer painted/molded furniture with bevel response, restrained metal/glass highlights on lamp/decor, and grounded contact shadows. Keep the premium rounded toy-game style, not photorealism.

Lift accent saturation toward the reference with controlled pink/purple/blue/yellow highlights while retaining v3's coherent pink/lilac base and cyan/gold accents. Avoid neon wash or high-frequency clutter.
Preserve a purposeful 390x844 derivative and do not bake character, buddy, navigation, counters, cards, text or runtime state into any environment asset.
